terms.definition: A small language made for one job, like describing screens or menus, inside a bigger language.

video.description:
Learn to explain result builders in Swift: Domain-Specific Language, Result Builder & buildBlock, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Domain-Specific Language - A small language made for one job, like describing screens or menus, inside a bigger language.
Result Builder - A type marked with `@resultBuilder` that turns a list of plain expressions into one combined result.
buildBlock - The static method in a Result Builder that combines all the parts of a block into one value.

landscape.title: Swift Result Builder, buildBlock & Domain-Specific Language | Day 46
landscape.description:
Explain Domain-Specific Language, Result Builder & buildBlock in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
도메인 특화 언어, 결과 빌더, buildBlock 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Domain-Specific Language - A small language made for one job, like describing screens or menus, inside a bigger language.
한국어: 도메인 특화 언어: 화면이나 메뉴를 표현하는 것처럼, 큰 언어 안에서 한 가지 일만을 위해 만든 작은 언어

Result Builder - A type marked with `@resultBuilder` that turns a list of plain expressions into one combined result.
한국어: 결과 빌더: @resultBuilder를 붙여, 평범한 표현식 목록을 하나로 합친 결과로 바꿔 주는 타입

buildBlock - The static method in a Result Builder that combines all the parts of a block into one value.
한국어: buildBlock: 결과 빌더 안에서 블록의 모든 부분을 하나의 값으로 합치는 static 메서드

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out how lines without commas become an array, what SwiftUI-style syntax is and why an if stopped compiling, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain result builders in English?

dialogue.title: Where are the commas?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `onboarding` has no commas and no brackets. How is it an array?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: `@Steps` is a Result Builder. It collects each line into one result.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Swift passes every string to buildBlock, and buildBlock returns the array.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So it's like a tiny Domain-Specific Language for steps?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. SwiftUI's view code is a Domain-Specific Language built the same way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cool. But I added an `if` for new users, and it stopped compiling.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: buildBlock alone can't handle an `if`. The Result Builder needs one more method.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. A Result Builder makes a Domain-Specific Language, and buildBlock glues the lines together.
SwiftUI code reads like a Domain-Specific Language.
